name: SB Energy, Inc.
headquarters: 3 Lagoon Dr., Suite 280, Redwood City, CA 94065, United States

ownership.type: subsidiary (SoftBank Group; IPO registration filed, unpriced)
ownership.notes: A Texas corporation since 28 August 2026, renamed SB Energy, Inc. on 31 August 2026. It has applied to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market and Nasdaq Texas under the symbol 'SBE'. The S-1 was filed on 1 September 2026 and amended on 4 and 21 September; as of 4 October 2026 no price range, share count or ownership percentage has been filed, and no 424B4 or Form 8-A. SoftBank expects to control more than 50% of the vote after the offering.

summary:
**BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** SB Energy is the SoftBank-controlled developer that will own the land, shells and power systems of OpenAI's largest leased campuses: Milam County, Texas (about 753 MW-IT, under construction) and PORTS-Pike, Ohio (about 8.0 GW-IT, leased to OpenAI on 17 August 2026, construction not started). It is a direct equipment buyer. Its S-1 says it procures solar modules, battery components, high-voltage transformers, switchgear and inverters itself, lets turnkey construction to EPC contractors, and has not yet selected the backup-generation engines for PORTS. The roughly 9.2 GW of gas generation planned beside PORTS is being developed by another SoftBank affiliate, not SB Energy. The IPO (Nasdaq and Nasdaq Texas: SBE) was filed on 1 September 2026 and is unpriced, with a delay over valuation reported in trade press.

**BACKGROUND.** Per its registration statement, SB Energy began in 2019 with SoftBank backing as a solar and storage developer. The registrant was formed as SE Global Holdings, LLC in Delaware in January 2024, became a Delaware corporation on 10 July 2026 and a Texas corporation on 28 August 2026, and took the name SB Energy, Inc. on 31 August 2026. It reports three segments: Data Centers, Standalone Power and Solutions. At 30 June 2026 it had about 2.2 GW of solar and battery storage operating (in CAISO and ERCOT), 2.5 GW under construction and 0.8 GW contracted. It states 8.8 GW-IT of data-centre capacity under lease, none yet in operation, and about USD 439bn of backlog, most of it PORTS. FY2025 revenue was USD 213.5m with a net loss attributable of USD 738.0m. H1 2026 revenue was USD 138.7m with a net loss of USD 3,208.9m, including a USD 2,573.1m non-cash charge on OpenAI's warrants. SoftBank has contributed about USD 3.2bn. OpenAI invested USD 500m of preferred equity in January 2026 and holds warrants. Affiliates of Ares hold USD 800m of preferred equity (about USD 996m of liquidation preference at 31 December 2025) and warrants in SBE Global, the direct parent; the S-1 says they are to be redeemed in full, and the warrants net-settled for about USD 40m, at or before the IPO, which the new credit facility requires. NVIDIA is putting in USD 3.0bn around the IPO and guarantees the first 4.25 GW-IT of the PORTS leases.
ecosystemRole: We assess SB Energy as the AIDC landlord in the corpus that is also its own power developer, and the only part of the SoftBank group that signs purchase orders for power equipment. Its scope runs 'to the rack': land, interconnection, the substation and switchyard packages, building shells, electrical and mechanical systems, and on-site or co-located generation. The tenant brings servers and GPUs. It buys owner-furnished equipment itself. It names Turner, DPR, Kiewit and SOLV Energy as its data-centre EPC providers, and SOLV, Blattner, Dashiell, CSI Electrical and Rosendin as its principal power EPCs, each on turnkey, fixed-scope contracts. Its storage fleet (Athos Storage with Fluence, Pelicans Jaw and Libra) makes it a battery buyer as well. Two constraints shape every sale: a CFIUS National Security Agreement that requires approval of certain vendors, and OpenAI's consent rights over 'materially important design contracts' on OpenAI-tenanted projects.

productsAndServices.name: Data Centers (DC) — powered AI campuses, delivered 'to the rack'
productsAndServices.description: SB Energy develops, builds and plans to operate gigawatt-scale data-centre campuses and leases them on triple-net terms. Its turnkey scope covers 'land, power, fiber, water, building shells and the critical internal systems … including mechanical, electrical and plumbing (“MEP”) systems, power distribution and cooling'. Customers 'bring their own racks and semiconductors'. Three campuses are leased: Cosmos in Austin (about 50 MW-IT, a SoftBank affiliate), Milam County, Texas (about 753 MW-IT across two buildings, OpenAI) and PORTS-Pike in Ohio (17 buildings of about 472 MW-IT each, about 8.0 GW-IT, OpenAI). 'No data center capacity is currently in operation.' Beyond the leased campuses it holds Borden and Scurry counties in ERCOT (about 1.7 GW-IT, with interconnection secured under Batch Zero) and a stated pipeline of about 30.6 GW-IT.
highlights: Leases are 15–20 years, with rent set on a yield-on-cost formula and escalating 2%–3% a year; cost overruns above an agreed cap are 'generally borne by us', though at PORTS they can be rentalized at a lower yield
PORTS: NVIDIA guarantees the OpenAI tenant's obligations on the first nine buildings (~4.25 GW-IT) up to USD 105bn
SB Energy claims designs with 'approximately 80% greater density than certain competing designs'
OpenAI holds consent and participation rights over 'specified materially important design contracts' on projects it leases (Foundation Agreement)
Studio 151, a data-centre construction-management firm, was bought in November 2025 for USD 12.0m
productsAndServices.positioning: The S-1 names Digital Realty, Equinix, QTS, Vantage, Switch, CyrusOne and Aligned as data-centre competitors, and says SB Energy is 'developing four of the seven largest data center sites by IT capacity in the United States'. Its distinguishing claim is owning the power development alongside the shell. Its concentration is the reverse: OpenAI and SoftBank are its tenants and investors.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Triple-net leases and service-level agreements signed directly with AI labs and hyperscalers; construction managed in-house and delivered by EPC contractors
productsAndServices.roadmap: Cosmos full RFS by May 2027; Milam buildings 2027–2028; PORTS first phase targeted for 2028, buildings 1–9 by 2031 and 10–17 by 2032, subject to approvals, financing and long-lead equipment

productsAndServices.name: Standalone Power (SP) — utility-scale solar and battery storage
productsAndServices.description: SB Energy develops, builds, owns and operates grid-connected solar and battery projects and sells their output under fixed-price power purchase agreements of 10–25 years. This segment 'currently generates substantially all of our revenue'. Operating capacity at 30 June 2026 was about 2.2 GW, mainly in ERCOT (~1,692 MWac of solar) and CAISO (~450 MWac). A further 2.5 GW was under construction and 0.8 GW contracted. Named projects include the Orion Solar Belt in Milam County (900 MWdc on SB Energy's site; 875 MWdc in its 2024 release; Google the anchor customer), Pelicans Jaw in Kern County, California (440 MWac solar plus 239 MW / 954 MWh of storage for San Diego Community Power), Libra in Nevada (700 MWac solar plus 700 MW / 2,800 MWh of storage for NV Energy) and Athos Storage in Riverside County, California (1.6 GWh, Fluence technology).
highlights: Battery storage under construction: Athos Storage 1.6 GWh (Fluence), Pelicans Jaw 954 MWh, Libra 2,800 MWh — no SB Energy battery is yet operating in California
First Solar thin-film modules: an original 1.7 GW plus a 1.5 GW multi-year order (2022), 3.2 GW cumulative
Orion I–III: First Solar modules, Nextracker trackers, Gerdau steel, Blattner as EPC (October 2024)
Stem named SB Energy's preferred energy-management partner for 10 GWh 'in principle' in November 2023; no deployment is on the record since
productsAndServices.positioning: S-1 competitors in power are Clearway, NextEra and AES. In 2022 SB Energy targeted 10 GW in operation or under construction by the end of 2025; the S-1 now reports 4.7 GWac developed, financed or begun since founding. Comparing those two company figures is our inference.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Fixed-price PPAs (largely 'as produced') with utilities, community choice aggregators and corporations; project debt, tax equity and construction-to-term loans
targetSegments: Load-serving entities (San Diego Community Power, NV Energy)
Merchant and capacity markets (CAISO resource adequacy, ERCOT)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Pelicans Jaw, Libra and Athos Storage under construction (financings closed March 2026); 6.9 GWac of standalone-power pipeline

productsAndServices.name: Co-located power for data centres
productsAndServices.description: SB Energy pairs its campuses with generation it develops. At Milam County it expects to deliver power from 'co-located power generation assets pursuant to on-site power supply agreements' and has 'developed more than 1.3 GW of incremental power generation capacity in Milam County'. Phased interconnection runs from Orion 1 at 34.5 kV and from Orion 2 and 3 at 345 kV, for an initial campus load of about 660 MW. It lists about 4.2 GWac of data-centre-dedicated power in its pipeline. At PORTS the gas generation is not SB Energy's: the S-1 says the roughly 9.2 GW of gas-fired plants are 'being developed by an affiliate of SoftBank that is not our subsidiary' and that SB Energy 'may provide development, construction management or operational services'.
highlights: The S-1 describes power configuration as 'grid-only, hybrid, behind-the-meter and bridge', chosen site by site
PORTS gas: no binding or non-binding agreement exists between SB Energy and any government entity; SB Energy says it has 'access to turbine reservations' (S-1 risk factor)
PORTS backup generation: 'the number and make/model of the backup generation engines' has not yet been selected
productsAndServices.positioning: Power-first development is what SB Energy sells to tenants against landlords that wait on the grid.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: On-site power supply agreements bundled into data-centre leases
productsAndServices.roadmap: Milam campus interconnection phases from August 2026 to March 2027

productsAndServices.name: Solutions (SLN) — design, engineering, construction management and operations
productsAndServices.description: The third reportable segment provides 'integrated design, engineering, construction management and operations management solutions to our SP and DC segments'. Its revenue is intersegment: USD 62.4m in FY2025 and USD 52.8m in H1 2026. It houses the construction organisation that 'leads construction management, vendor selection, contract administration and on-site oversight', and Studio 151's data-centre delivery team of more than 50 people.
highlights: Power EPC packages are split three ways: PV and battery installation; the 'high-voltage switchyard and interconnection facilities'; and BESS balance of plant
EPC protections: delay and capacity liquidated damages, two-to-three-year warranties, serial-defect replacement, parent guarantees
targetSegments: SB Energy's own DC and SP projects

strategyRead: **(High confidence)** We assess that **SB Energy is a direct, portfolio-scale buyer of long-lead electrical equipment**. The S-1 says it procures 'solar modules, battery energy storage system components, high-voltage transformers, switchgear, inverters' as owner-furnished equipment. It procures 'early, at portfolio scale and across multiple suppliers', in arrangements meant to let equipment be 'reallocated across sites'. Its capex estimates rest on 'executed purchase orders, vendor bids, framework arrangements'. Basis: S-1/A2, procurement and execution-model sections. A seller qualifies with the supply-chain team as a framework supplier, not project by project.

**(High confidence)** We assess that **the PORTS gas plant is not SB Energy's purchase, but the campus's own electrical and backup systems are**. The S-1 says the roughly 9.2 GW of gas-fired generation is being developed by a SoftBank affiliate that is not its subsidiary, which SB Energy does 'not expect to own or operate'. Separately, the campus needs 'gas turbines, transformers, power electronics, heating-ventilation-and air conditioning systems and modular data center elements', and the backup-generation engines have not been chosen. The DOE fact sheet and SB Energy's own PORTS microsite describe the gas ownership differently; the S-1 is the document under securities liability.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **OpenAI is SB Energy's customer, investor and design gatekeeper at once**, which narrows the specification for any equipment sold into Milam and PORTS. OpenAI leases about 8.8 GW-IT, holds USD 500m of preferred equity and warrants, designates a director, and under the Foundation Agreement holds consent and participation rights over 'materially important design contracts' on its projects. Basis: S-1/A2, related-party section. Inference: on OpenAI-tenanted campuses, a power-architecture choice such as an SST or 800 VDC distribution would need OpenAI's agreement as well as SB Energy's.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **SB Energy's battery buying is real and current, while its data-centre buying is still mostly ahead of it**. Athos Storage (1.6 GWh, Fluence), Pelicans Jaw (954 MWh) and Libra (2,800 MWh) are financed and under construction. On the data-centre side only about 0.8 GW-IT of the 8.8 GW-IT portfolio is under construction, and PORTS has not started. Basis: S-1/A2 project status tables and the March 2026 financings.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **the IPO's timing is the main near-term swing factor for SB Energy's ability to fund PORTS**. It targets about 90% debt and 10% equity at PORTS and says the transmission build alone could need more than USD 6bn of credit support. IFR reports the roadshow on hold over a valuation gap below USD 50bn (reported). Basis: S-1/A2 financing sections; IFR. An IPO that prices proceeds as planned; a long delay leaves NVIDIA's guarantee and SoftBank's support carrying the equity.

**(Low confidence)** We assess that **the CFIUS vendor-approval regime will favour suppliers already on SB Energy's approved lists**. The National Security Agreement requires approval or non-objection for certain vendor relationships, and SB Energy keeps 'approved vendor lists for SCADA, networking and other critical operational technology systems'. It says the rules have delayed onboarding. Weak because the S-1 does not say which equipment classes are covered beyond operational technology.

**Collection gaps:** no equipment supplier is named anywhere in the S-1 (First Solar, Nextracker and Fluence appear only on SB Energy's website); the OEMs for Pelicans Jaw and Libra storage; the name and ownership of the SoftBank affiliate developing the PORTS gas and who holds the turbine reservations; ownership percentages after the IPO; whether AEP Ohio's definitive agreements for the 9.2 GW were signed in Q3 2026; how 'Customer D' (29% of FY2025 revenue) is named; the gap between AEP's USD 4.2bn and the S-1's USD 5.1bn of PORTS grid investment, which may count different scopes.

**INDICATORS TO WATCH** — *424B4 / Form 8-A:* pricing sets SoftBank's and OpenAI's stakes and funds the equity for PORTS. *AEP Ohio's Q3 2026 results (late October):* executed agreements would move 9.2 GW of service toward OPSB, FERC and PUCO review. *OPSB local public hearing on the Baku–Gavin 765 kV line, 27 October 2026:* the first public test of the transmission route. *Milam County Building 1 delivery (2027):* SB Energy's first data hall in operation. *Any award for PORTS backup generation or switchgear:* the first named data-centre equipment order. *Athos Storage in service (TB4 contracts effective 1 December 2026):* SB Energy's first operating California battery.

relationships.scale: ~USD 3.2bn of cash contributions; >50% of the vote expected after the IPO
relationships.via: SB Energy HoldCo, LLC and SVF II Energy (DE) LLC
relationships.note: Founding sponsor and ultimate parent; SoftBank designates six of nine directors, and a SoftBank affiliate is the tenant at the Cosmos campus.
relationships.context: The S-1 names SoftBank its 'founding sponsor and ultimate parent company' and says its affiliates have contributed about USD 3.2bn. After the offering SoftBank expects to control more than 50% of the vote, making SB Energy a controlled company. It designates William Bice, Alex Clavel (chairman), Ron Fisher, Kimberly Johnson, Seiichi Morooka and Alexi Wellman. SB Energy pays SoftBank a royalty of 1% of gross profit for the 'SB Energy' name. A SoftBank affiliate leases the Cosmos campus for 15 years under a SoftBank Group Capital guarantee of about USD 2.9bn. The roughly 9.2 GW of PORTS gas generation is being developed by another SoftBank affiliate.

relationships.note: Tenant of the Milam County campus (15-year leases, January 2026) and the PORTS-Pike campus (17 leases of 20 years, August 2026); also a USD 500m preferred investor with warrants and a board seat.
relationships.context: On 9 January 2026 an OpenAI affiliate (Orion DC I, LLC) signed two leases for Milam County Buildings 1 and 2 (about 308 and 445 MW-IT), and OpenAI invested USD 500m of preferred equity in Energy Global. SB Energy's release said OpenAI and SoftBank were each investing USD 500m 'to Advance Stargate'. On 17 August 2026 an OpenAI affiliate signed 17 leases covering about 8.0 GW-IT at PORTS-Pike. OpenAI holds 3,991,809 warrants (pre-split) vesting on milestones and valuation thresholds; their fair value was about USD 5.5bn at 30 June 2026. It designates director Sachin Katti and holds consent rights over materially important design contracts on its projects. The S-1 itself never uses the word 'Stargate'.

relationships.scale: USD 3.0bn (USD 1.5bn prepaid forward funded; USD 1.5bn Class N at the IPO); guaranties up to USD 105bn
relationships.via: Class N common stock; residual value guaranties at PORTS-Pike
relationships.note: Investor and credit support at PORTS-Pike: NVIDIA prepaid USD 1.5bn, commits USD 1.5bn more at the IPO, guarantees the OpenAI tenant's obligations on the first ~4.25 GW-IT, and is the campus's exclusive compute provider.
relationships.context: SB Energy's 17 August 2026 release says NVIDIA will be 'the exclusive AI compute infrastructure provider at PORTS-Pike' and will provide credit support on the initial 4.25 GW-IT, with an option on the rest. The S-1 adds that NVIDIA funded USD 1.5bn under a prepaid forward on 17 August 2026, at 90% of the IPO price. It is committed to buy USD 1.5bn of non-voting Class N stock in a concurrent private placement. Its residual value guaranties carry an aggregate cap of USD 105bn. SB Energy pays NVIDIA nothing for them; OpenAI compensates NVIDIA separately.

relationships.scale: USD 800m of preferred equity issued (≈USD 996m liquidation preference at 31 Dec 2025) plus warrants
relationships.note: Affiliates of Ares Management hold preferred equity and warrants in SBE Global, SB Energy's direct parent, with senior economic rights and no board seat; the S-1 says they are redeemed in full at the IPO.
relationships.context:
The S-1/A2 defines Ares as 'affiliates of Ares Management Corporation that hold preferred equity interests and warrants of SBE Global, including Ares SBE SPV, L.P.'. SBE Global issued USD 800m of preferred equity to Ares across 2022, 2024 and 2025, with an aggregate liquidation preference of about USD 996m at 31 December 2025, and warrants with the 2025 issuance; part of an earlier tranche was redeemed for USD 495.0m in the first half of 2025. The preferred equity is 'not an obligation of, or equity interest in, SB Energy, Inc.'

At the IPO, SBE Global is to redeem the preferred equity in full and net-settle the warrants for about USD 40m, after which 'Ares will no longer hold any equity interest, preferred claim, or warrant position in SBE Global or any of its subsidiaries'. The Ares Redemption is a condition of the new credit facility. Board designation and consent rights in the post-IPO shareholders' agreement go to SoftBank and OpenAI only.

relationships.scale: USD 4.2bn of transmission paid for by SB Energy (AEP); ~USD 5.1bn of AEP capital costs passed through (S-1)
relationships.via: AEP Ohio Electric Service Agreement (0.8 GW) and 765 kV transmission for PORTS-Pike
relationships.note: AEP Ohio serves PORTS-Pike: an Electric Service Agreement covers 0.8 GW, and service for a further 9.2 GW, with the 765 kV build SB Energy pays for, awaits definitive agreements and OPSB, FERC and PUCO approvals.
relationships.context: AEP's 20 March 2026 release says 'SB Energy is committed to paying for the $4.2 billion in new transmission investments' for a 10 GW campus, with power expected from 2029. The S-1 records an Electric Service Agreement and Letter of Agreement with AEP Ohio for 0.8 GW. It says agreements for the 9.2 GW of transmission capacity are 'at various stages of execution and are subject to final regulatory approvals'. It puts AEP's capital costs at about USD 5.1bn, passed through to SB Energy with a regulated return, and the credit support needed at more than USD 6bn. On 30 July 2026 AEP still called SB Energy the 'prospective offtaker'. The USD 4.2bn and USD 5.1bn figures may cover different scopes; no source reconciles them.

relationships.scale: 700 MWac solar + 700 MW / 2,800 MWh storage; 25-year PPA
relationships.note: NV Energy, a Berkshire Hathaway Energy utility, buys the output of SB Energy's Libra solar-plus-storage project in Nevada under a fixed-price 25-year PPA.
relationships.context: The S-1 describes Libra, in Mineral and Lyon counties, Nevada, as '700 MWac (910 MWdc) of PV and 700 MW / 2,800 MWh of BESS' with 'a fixed-price 25-year PPA with NV Energy'. It is SB Energy's largest solar-plus-storage hybrid, financed with a USD 2.4bn construction and bridge commitment on 13 March 2026 and under construction.

It named First Solar modules, Nextracker trackers, Gerdau steel and Blattner as EPC. SB Energy's projects page lists Google as Orion's anchor customer at 900 MWdc. policyExposure.exposure: SoftBank and certain subsidiaries entered into a National Security Agreement with CFIUS on 23 December 2019 over SoftBank's ownership of SB Energy's US operations, supplemented on 20 September 2021. It imposes 'restrictions on vendors, cybersecurity requirements and project sale notification procedures', including approval or non-objection for certain vendor relationships. SB Energy says these restrictions 'have delayed, and may continue to delay, our ability to onboard vendors'.
policyExposure.mitigation: SB Energy maintains 'approved vendor lists for SCADA, networking and other critical operational technology systems deployed at our project sites'.

policyExposure.exposure: Under the 2025 tax law, solar projects must have begun construction on or before 4 July 2026 or be placed in service by 31 December 2027 to qualify for the 45Y/48E credits. Projects beginning construction after 31 December 2025 must meet the new foreign-entity-of-concern rules. SB Energy says it is not an FEOC and does not expect to become one, but that 'these regulations may nonetheless be applicable to us'. It notes that a significant portion of its panels, inverters, transformers, turbines and batteries is made outside the United States.
policyExposure.mitigation: SB Energy says 'the large majority of our current solar and battery energy storage pipeline has satisfied applicable safe harbor requirements', and it structures projects for the energy-community and domestic-content ITC adders.

policyExposure.regime: DOE emergency order on foreign bulk-power equipment
policyExposure.exposure: The S-1 records that on 26 August 2026 an emergency order allowed the DOE to prohibit 'the acquisition, importation, transfer or installation of foreign-produced bulk-power equipment' involving a covered foreign entity. SB Energy says it does 'not yet know the impact', and that if required to change suppliers 'we may be unable to do so'.

policyExposure.regime: Texas large-load rules (SB 6) and ERCOT Batch Zero
policyExposure.exposure: SB Energy's Borden and Scurry county sites (about 1.7 GW-IT) hold interconnection under ERCOT's Batch Zero Base Load designation, 'subject to confirmation under the ERCOT large-load verification process', and Texas energization remains subject to ERCOT and PUCT audit. Its Milam campus site says that 'in accordance with SB6, the project will pay for interconnection costs and shed load first during times of emergency'.
policyExposure.mitigation: SB Energy wrote to Governor Abbott on 7 August 2026 supporting large-load transparency and accountability.
